top_choice_rationale: P001, a single-writer award to Mircea Cărtărescu, is the proposal that best meets the common criteria. Public knowledge and translated reception of Blinding, the Orbitor trilogy and Solenoid suggest a voice that is hard to confuse with any other, formal and linguistic ambition sustained at very large scale, and imaginative depth that builds memory, the body and dream into one metaphysical architecture. Attribution is clean: one author, one principal language. The round-2 exchange narrowed the citation to the prose anchored in the Orbitor trilogy and Solenoid, because no member has assessed the poetry and early work. Open uncertainties remain. The Romanian syntax, rhythm and density can be judged only through translation. It is also unproven whether the later novels transform the project or only extend it. These uncertainties are weighed against a no-award outcome, and they do not outweigh the case. I do not treat the unanimity of the openings as merit. Alternatives such as Adonis and Zurita were not on the slate and faced larger, unequal evidentiary gaps in Arabic and Spanish. P000 is ranked last because the supplied evidence supports a defensible, appropriately scoped single-laureate recommendation.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile. As chair I wrote the round-1 summary while also supporting B007, and I disclose that dual role. My scholarly and poetic work is context, not evidence of preference, and the profile lists no tie to Cărtărescu.
